Maladaptive Strategies.value: Going to or near the place where the event happened
Being around people in authority or uniform

Threat.value: I often react as if I am in danger even when nothing is actually wrong
I constantly scan my surroundings for signs of danger
I only feel safe in a very limited number of places

Negative Appraisals.value: What happened to me was deeply unfair and nothing has been done about it
The event happened because of the way I acted
I will never be able to feel normal emotions again

This makes that item look clinically disconnected rather than merely unusual.

issues.explanation: Compulsive cleaning can occur after sexual assault, but in this profile it is not supported by the other selected items or the formulation. vignette:
Omar was a 54-year-old software engineer who lived alone in a small apartment in a bustling city. Despite his professional success, Omar’s life had taken a turn into a shadowy realm since the night of his assault. It was a few years ago now, but the memories haunted him as vividly as if they had happened yesterday. That evening, he had been walking home from a late meeting when he was confronted by a group of men. What began as a simple act of walking became a nightmare that would ripple through his life in ways he never anticipated. The fear and humiliation of that encounter left him feeling exposed and vulnerable, particularly when he recalled the sound of sirens in the distance, echoing through the streets like a cruel reminder of his experience.

In the days and weeks that followed, Omar found himself increasingly unable to cope. The once-familiar streets around his home began to feel like a minefield. He noticed that he became jumpy at the sound of an ambulance siren, which would send his heart racing, forcing him to relive that moment of terror. Even the sight of a police uniform would trigger an overwhelming sense of dread. He began to isolate himself, choosing to stay indoors or avoid any social gatherings where men would be present. He felt safest in his apartment, surrounded by the soft glow of his computer screen, where he could immerse himself in coding and data. But he was aware that this avoidance came at a cost—his relationships with friends and family began to suffer. Invitations to dinner or outings with colleagues were turned down, each excuse more flimsy than the last. He was terrified of being confronted by authority figures, convinced that their presence would remind him of his vulnerability.

Omar’s internal world was fraught with turmoil. He often found himself scanning his surroundings, alert for any sign of potential danger, even in seemingly mundane settings. While waiting in line at the grocery store, he would lock his gaze on the door, half-expecting someone to burst in. His mind became a relentless machine of worst-case scenarios, leading him to react as if danger loomed at every corner, even when he was surrounded by friends who meant him no harm. At work, he struggled to concentrate, his mind drifting to thoughts of injustice and self-blame. What haunted him most was the belief that somehow, he had brought this upon himself, that his actions that night had contributed to the assault. These thoughts gnawed at him, making it difficult for him to trust himself or others.

As months turned into years, Omar’s emotional landscape shifted. He felt numb and distanced from the world around him, believing that he would never be able to feel normal emotions again. Laughter felt foreign, and joy seemed like a distant memory. The weight of his trauma pressed heavily on his chest, leaving him feeling isolated. He had come to believe that nothing could change, that he was forever altered by that night and would never reclaim the life he once knew. 

It was during a particularly challenging week at work, when a new project required collaboration with a male colleague, that Omar reached a breaking point. The anxiety of being in the same room with another man, coupled with the pressure of deadlines, led him to a near-panic attack. He excused himself, retreating to the restroom for what felt like an eternity, grappling with the reality that he could no longer function in his job without succumbing to overwhelming fear. 

Finally, one day, a friend reached out, expressing concern over Omar’s well-being and urging him to seek help. The thought of therapy had crossed his mind before, but he had always dismissed it, believing that he should be able to handle things on his own. Yet, standing in the bathroom, trembling and gasping for breath, he realized that perhaps he could not do this alone. What frightened him most was the uncertainty of what lay ahead. Would he be able to confront his past? Would he find a way to feel safe again? As he made the decision to seek help, a flicker of hope ignited within him, a small but significant step towards reclaiming his life from the shadows that had enveloped him for too long.
